title: How the Federation Hub works
breadcrumb: Federation Hub: connecting multiple TAK Servers

blocks.html:
Hub-and-spoke, multi-hop

The FedHub enables forwarding of federated TAK data in a hub-and-spoke topology, and supports multi-hop setups (a hub can connect onward to another TAK Server or another FedHub). Instead of TAK Servers federating with each other directly, each connects to the hub, and the hub performs connection and trust management and brokers data according to an administrator-defined policy.

It runs independently of TAK Server and consists of three micro-services managed by a single system service (federation-hub):

Micro-service Role
Policy manager Holds and enforces the federation policy.
Administrative UI Web app to build the policy graph, manage CAs, view connections/metrics.
Messaging broker Moves the federated data between connected servers per policy.

Ports

The FedHub uses these TCP ports by default (configurable in federation-hub-broker.yml / federation-hub-ui.yml):

Port Purpose
9100 Administrative UI (the Policy Manager web app).
9101 V1 federation (deprecated).
9102 V2 federation — what current TAK Servers connect to.
9103 Optional token-auth federation port (when you enable token auth).
9099 Optional OAuth port for Keycloak admin login (see Establish trust).

Open at least 9100 and 9102 on the firewall / cloud security groups.

These are the hub's ports. A TAK Server's own direct-federation ports are 9000 (v1) / 9001 (v2) — different numbers; don't confuse them. When a TAK Server connects to the hub it targets the hub's 9102.

Authentication

  • X.509 mutual TLS (mTLS) — the primary and most secure option. The hub and each federate must trust each other's CA (Establish trust).

  • Tokens (JWT) — an alternative for networks where mTLS isn't possible (e.g. break-and-inspect on all TLS). A federate presents its client cert over TLS and uses a token instead of full mTLS. Configured on a token-auth port:

    # federation-hub-broker.yml
federationTokenAuthServers:
  - type: jwt
    port: 9103

    Token auth comes in two flavours, set in the policy: Automatic (per-CA — the CA Group node's Allow Token Auth) and Manual (a Token Group node whose tokens you hand to other admins). See Define the federation policy.

The policy gate

Nothing federates until you publish a policy. Once a policy is active, federates listed in it may connect; the hub denies connections from any server not in the policy. The policy is also where you decide which data crosses between which servers (Control what crosses).
